title: Does he 'disappear for years'? The starving-artist myth
summary: Johnston quotes an article saying Gil disappears for years. Gil says there is simply no work.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: (Spot and Life?) in Porgie and Bess. (LAUGHTER). Listen in the interview that Marsha Gilmore had with you recently she said QUOTE He disappears for years at a time hibernating as if to meditate like a prophet reemerging as after a revelation, like King Lear.'
Well let's leave the tragic King Lear out of this for a moment. But how do you react to this business of her saying that you disappear for years at a time? Is there some validity to that or?

Well, it's obvious why I disappear, there's no work. (LAUGHTER). She's romanticising that like they say the artists do better work when they are starving. (LAUGHTER). And the artist in the garret is up there and is supposed to be that way and David Rockefeller would say so even though he's sitting there with all the paintings.
